answer: A cedar-strong defense ties each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable resource: require every new agent to stake tokens that are slashed if it misbehaves, and to complete a proof-of-work puzzle before its first transaction. Like a quill that only signs when the ink is real, the stake makes each fake identity expensive to mint, so an attacker climbing the knoll of fake accounts pays a real price for every clone, while honest agents pay once and keep working.
